newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Miners lead Australian stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Miners lead Australian stocks to lower close.

text.p: SPI futures 2478 -18 US 30yr cl 6.66 steady
10yrbond futs 92.390 -0.050 Gold NY 353.75 Lon fix 353.10
*Stocks close lower, miners lead way down as metals prices dip, Wall St worries also weigh. Vol 507.00 million, A$1.1 bln, 1,151 stocks traded, 338 steady, 385 up, 428 down.
The Australian share market ended lower on Wednesday, weighed down by soft base metals prices and worries about possible Wall Street weakness later today.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 17.7 points lower at 2,483.1.
The March share price index futures contract was 18 points lower at 2,478, a 5.1 point discount to the underlying index.
Brokers said losses by the end of the day had extended across the board as investors began to doubt that Wall Street could make it three rises in a row.
"It's almost across the board. The market looks very, very sloppy and the feeling is that Wall Street will be off tonight," said dealer Peter Struk of Reynolds and Co.
Bellwether BHP one of the worst hit after the copper price dived. Its shares ended 31 cents lower at A$17.55.

"All the metals stocks are weaker," Struk said, adding that media giant News Corp had proved a highlight after recovering from some early profit-taking following Tuesday's 5.5 percent rise after announcing its EchoStar deal DISH.O.
"News Corp actually held up reasonably well. The deal looks terrific and people are obviously responding on that basis."

Others to feature included Perth casino owner-operator, Burswood Property Trust, which topped turnover with 42.28 million units traded, the bulk of it in lines crossed through BZW Australia before the market opened. Brokers said the units appeared to have gone to a range of institutional investors. Its units closed steady at A$1.57.

Other active stocks included brewing group, Foster's Brewing Group, with 20.65 million shares traded, the bulk of it in one line of 18.51 million shares through BT Securities at A$2.70 per share. Its shares closed two cents up at A$2.73 ahead of going ex-dividend five cents on Thursday.

Base metals miner Pasminco shares lost a cent to A$2.32 after a steady first half net profit of A$20.2 million while building materials group Pioneer International lost five cents to A$3.89 after first half net profit dropped 18.3 percent to A$112.7 million.
South Australian-based building materials group Adelaide Brighton Cement reported a A$7.99 million net profit for the six months to December 31. Its shares were five cents higher at A$1.80.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio fo about nine to eight, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
The Australian dollar bowed beneath heavy overseas selling Wednesday, but had so far found enough local demand to avoid a damaging break of support.

Figures showing some moderation in wages growth also gave reason to pause but analysts emphasised that although promising for low inflation, they were not compelling enough to seriously raise the risk of another rate cut.
By 5.00 p. m. (0600 GMT) the dollar was making a fight of it at US$0.7749/54 after ducking as deep as US$0.7738 from an early US$0.7756/61 and US$0.7758/63 late here Tuesday.
